annotation.title_clean: The Medical Devices (Post-market Surveillance Requirements) (Amendment) (Great Britain) Regulations 2024
annotation.title_en: The Medical Devices (Post-market Surveillance Requirements) (Amendment) (Great Britain) Regulations 2024
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department of Health and Social Care (UK Secretary of State); published by King's Printer of Acts of Parliament
annotation.summary_en: UK statutory instrument amending the Medical Devices Regulations 2002 to add a new Part 4A on post-market surveillance for medical devices in Great Britain. It requires manufacturers to run surveillance systems and plans, report serious incidents and trends, take field safety corrective actions, and keep records. It has no AI or robotics-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Manufacturers must maintain a risk-proportionate post-market surveillance system based on a PMS plan.
Serious incidents must be reported within 15 days (2 days for public health threats, 10 days for death or unanticipated serious deterioration).
Field safety corrective actions require a risk assessment, a report and field safety notices to the Secretary of State.
Periodic safety update reports or PMS reports are required, with frequency depending on device class.
Documentation must be kept for 10 years (15 for implantables), and the regulator can demand it within 3 working days.
